in_english.name: Nauroz
in_english.meaning: Persian New Year and spring beginning
in_english.long_meaning: Nauroz, also known as Nowruz, marks the beginning of the Persian New Year and spring, symbolizing renewal and hope. Etymologically derived from the Persian words 'nav' meaning 'new' and 'roz' meaning 'day', it signifies a fresh start. With ancient roots, Nauroz holds significant cultural and spiritual importance in Islamic and Persian traditions, reflecting themes of rejuvenation, harmony with nature, and community celebration.

data.cultural_impact: Nauroz is celebrated as the Persian New Year and is one of the oldest holidays in the world, with roots dating back to ancient Iranian civilizations. Traditions include cleaning the house, wearing new clothes, preparing festive meals, visiting the graves of loved ones, and gathering with family and friends for feasts and parties. Nauroz is a time for renewing relationships, being generous to others, and setting new goals for the coming year.
data.spiritual_significance: The term Nauroz is derived from the Persian words for "new day" and "new life," reflecting the spiritual beliefs of renewal and new beginnings. Muslims mark the arrival of Nauroz with religious observances, such as offering special prayers, reading from the holy Qur'an, and seeking forgiveness from Allah. This day also serves as a reminder of the importance of living a virtuous life and striving for personal growth and self-improvement, in accordance with Islamic teachings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "New Day" symbolizes A day of renewal and happiness. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Nauroz serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of new day.
